summary: Filed a successor of the live-cluster experiment that adds the healing phase, because the current account still lists the post-healing fate of the conflicting entry and the long-run persistence of the stale membership as unobserved. The fixture, restart, partition, admission and the seven earlier comparisons are carried over unchanged; after the split-brain sample the harness now reconnects the full mesh, waits for one leader, applies one more entry and emits a fourth event sampling each node's payload and term at the conflicted index plus the restarted node's configuration and log progress. Three comparisons were added: entry payloads at that index must be consistent, the restarted node must report the committed membership once the cluster is whole and committing, and its log must have advanced as a progress control. Local construction feedback was stable across four runs on those three fields (A and C keep minority-write while B, D and E keep majority-write at the same index and term, so the entries cannot be reconciled by term comparison; the restarted node stays at {A,B,C} while its log advances; the cluster keeps committing), while the healed leader's identity varied (A once, D or E three times), so no comparison asserts on it and that operand is recorded only. Incomplete: this successor's receipt and interpretation, the no-feature restart control inside the cluster, the earlier constructor replay-backpressure question, and whether a snapshot install or compaction eventually repairs the divergent entries.
